author_lineage: xyflow team; official React Flow documentation on next.reactflow.dev.
edition: Mutable next documentation; page reports last updated 2026-10-08; immutable release unknown.
exact_section: Using multiple handles, lines 410-427; Dynamic handles, lines 471-473.
confirmed: Distinct handle IDs and endpoint references address separate connection points. CSS can position handles along a side. Changing handle counts or positions requires refreshing node internals.
limits: No automatic count-based spacing algorithm is supplied; route separation away from endpoints is not guaranteed.
counter_observation: Default handles occupy the center of their side, so several IDs alone do not separate endpoints.

limits: This establishes insertion behavior, not curve routing or automatic spacing.
counter_observation: Changing only an edge ID cannot solve this duplicate-insertion case.

exact_section: Spacing Combinations, lines 16-42; Individual Spacings, lines 51-54; Remarks, lines 55-58.

limits: No React Flow integration or exact routed fixture is provided here.
counter_observation: A configured centerline gap does not directly equal visible clearance between thick strokes.

author_lineage: Eclipse Layout Kernel project; official option reference.
edition: Current mutable option reference; version and publication date unknown.
exact_section: Additional Documentation, lines 21-31, especially PORTS_OVERHANG and UNIFORM_PORT_SPACING.
confirmed: A uniform-spacing option compensates for gaps made unequal by differently sized labels. Overhang preserves requested port spacing beyond node boundaries when space is insufficient.
limits: Behavior depends on a supporting layout and sizing configuration; no running React Flow example was inspected.
counter_observation: Without overhang, crowded nodes may violate the requested port gap.
